title: Protocol-based remote messaging for interactive sessions
references: Operator request 2026-11-13: a remote chat client must send and read messages without typing into the terminal
Spike 2026-11-13: Claude TUI <-> stream-json --resume handoff; Codex app-server shared by the TUI (--remote) and a second JSON-RPC client

needs: Let a remote chat client deliver a message to a running interactive cdx session through a supported provider protocol instead of typing into the terminal.
Expose the session's turn state and replies from the provider protocol instead of hooks and screen scraping.
Keep the interactive terminal usable: the operator can always take the session back from the keyboard.
context: Remote clients currently paste text into a terminal multiplexer pane and infer state from the screen; prompts, busy turns, fresh sessions and interrupts each produced a distinct failure mode.
cdx already owns the provider process: _run_interactive_provider_process in src/provider_runtime.py starts the TUI as a child and waits for it, and agent_state records hook events per session.

Claude spike: a conversation started in the TUI was continued with `claude -p --resume <id> --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose`; the run used subscription auth (apiKeySource none), wrote to the same transcript file (entrypoint sdk-cli), and a TUI reopened with --resume rendered every turn and kept the context.

Codex spike: `codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` served the TUI started with `codex --remote` and a second JSON-RPC client; the client listed the loaded thread, resumed it, started a turn, received turn/started, item/* and turn/completed, and the TUI rendered the remote turn live.
Codex refuses a Unix socket whose parent directory is writable by other users; its WebSocket transport is marked experimental.
Claude Code fires no Stop hook on an Esc interrupt, so hook-derived state can stay 'working' after an interrupt.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: `cdx send <session> <text>` delivers the text to a running interactive Claude or Codex session launched with the feature enabled, without writing to its terminal input.

AC2: For Claude, the launcher switches from the TUI to a stream-json --resume run on the same conversation when a message arrives while the TUI is idle, queues it while a TUI turn is running, and returns to the TUI with --resume on a keypress; no turn or context is lost across switches.

AC3: For Codex, the launcher starts an app-server bound to a private endpoint and attaches the TUI with --remote; `cdx send` starts a turn on the TUI's thread as a second client and the TUI renders it live.

AC4: Each session writes an append-only event log (JSON lines) with turn states (working, done, waiting, permission, interrupted, failed) and assistant text taken from the provider protocol; `cdx send --interrupt` interrupts the current remote turn.

AC5: The control endpoint accepts only the session owner: a private Unix socket in a 0700 directory on Linux and macOS, and a loopback endpoint guarded by a per-session secret on Windows; no secret appears in argv, logs or the event log.
AC6: With the feature disabled, launch, resume and headless behaviour are byte-for-byte unchanged, and existing tests pass.

AC7: Automated tests cover the switch loop, queueing, interrupt, endpoint access control and event mapping with fake providers on Linux, macOS and Windows, plus a documented live check against the real CLIs on each platform.

product.title: Remote control of interactive sessions through provider protocols
product.overview: cdx lets a remote chat client drive the same interactive session the operator sees in the terminal, using the providers' own programmatic interfaces.
goals: Reliable message delivery and state for remote clients, with no terminal typing or screen parsing.
One conversation shared between the terminal and the remote client, with the keyboard always able to take it back.
Identical behaviour on Linux, macOS and Windows.
non_goals: Building the remote client user interface.
Supporting providers other than Claude and Codex in this delivery.
Exposing the control endpoint beyond the local machine.

backlog_items.title: Add a private per-session control endpoint and the cdx send command
problem: Remote clients have no supported way to reach a running interactive session.
Unix sockets are not available on every Windows setup, and Codex rejects sockets in shared directories.
scope_in: An opt-in launch setting that creates the endpoint for the lifetime of the interactive launcher.
A small line-delimited JSON request protocol: send, interrupt, status.
`cdx send <session> <text>` and `cdx send --interrupt`, with clear errors when the session is not running or not enabled.
scope_out: Provider-specific delivery, handled by the next items.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: `cdx send` reaches the launcher of a running enabled session and reports delivery or a precise error.
AC5: The endpoint is owner-only on every platform and never exposes its secret.
AC6: Disabled sessions launch exactly as before.

backlog_items.title: Switch Claude sessions between the TUI and a stream-json resume run
problem: Claude Code has no attach mode: a second writer must continue the conversation with --resume while the TUI is closed.
scope_in: A local/remote loop around the interactive Claude child: idle detection from the session's own hook state, graceful TUI exit, a stream-json --resume run fed from the endpoint, and a keypress return to the TUI with --resume.
Queueing of messages received while a TUI turn is running.
Event mapping from stream-json (system, assistant, result, error) to the event log, and interrupt of the remote run.
scope_out: Permission prompts inside remote runs beyond the session's configured permission mode.
acceptance_criteria: AC2: A conversation keeps its context across TUI -> remote -> TUI, on the same conversation id.
AC4: The event log records working, done, interrupted and failed states and the assistant text of remote turns.

backlog_items.title: Share a Codex app-server between the TUI and remote clients
problem: Codex can serve several clients on one thread, but cdx launches its TUI standalone.
scope_in: Launch `codex app-server` on a private endpoint and the TUI with --remote for enabled sessions, with clean shutdown of both.
A minimal JSON-RPC client (initialize, thread/loaded/list, thread/resume, turn/start, turn/interrupt) used by the launcher to deliver messages.
Event mapping from turn and item notifications to the event log.
scope_out: Approval requests from the app-server beyond the session's configured approval policy.
acceptance_criteria: AC3: A message sent with cdx send runs on the TUI's thread and is rendered live in the TUI.
AC4: The event log records turn states and agent text from notifications.

backlog_items.title: Prove the remote messaging loop on Linux, macOS and Windows
problem: Process control, sockets and terminals differ per platform; a Linux-only proof would not hold.
scope_in: Fake-provider tests for the switch loop, queue, interrupt, endpoint access and event mapping, run in CI on the three platforms.
A documented live check script against the real Claude and Codex CLIs, run once per platform before release.
acceptance_criteria: AC6: Existing suites stay green with the feature disabled.
AC7: The new tests pass on the three platforms and the live check is recorded for each.

orchestration_task.title: Implement protocol-based remote messaging for interactive sessions
plan: Read provider_runtime launch paths, agent_state and conversation readers; confirm the invariants the feature must not change when disabled.
Build the control endpoint, request protocol and cdx send command with owner-only access per platform.
Add the Claude local/remote switch loop with queueing, interrupt and event mapping.
Add the Codex shared app-server launch and JSON-RPC client with event mapping.
Write fake-provider tests, run them on Linux, macOS and Windows, run the live check per platform, and document usage and limits.
